turns.content: Relabel five arbitrary real numbers so that a1<=a2<=a3<=a4<=a5. We seek the least universal C such that some two ratios using four distinct indices differ by at most C. Define r1=a1/a2, r2=a3/a4, r3=a1/a5, r4=a2/a3, and r5=a4/a5. Why does each ratio lie in (0,1]?
Encode an edge between two of these ratios when they use four distinct original indices. What graph is formed by the five consecutive pairs in the cyclic order r1,r2,r3,r4,r5?
Check each of the five cycle edges explicitly and verify that the two endpoint ratios use four distinct indices.
Color the five ratios and determine what the cycle would imply if every edge joined different colors.
Use the graph you obtained to decide whether every edge can join different colors. What does that imply about finding an admissible pair in a single color class?
Use your graph and coloring argument to obtain a universal upper bound for the difference of two ratios with four distinct indices.
For large N, determine the smallest gap obtainable from two admissible ratios and its limiting value.
Combine the universal bound with the sharpness family to determine the smallest possible constant C.
